case_name: Ram Murti and Another v State of Haryana
respondent:
State of Haryana
Supreme Court of India

14 September 1976
Cr.A. No. 288 of 1971 (Arising as an appeal by Special Leave from the Judgment and Order Dt. 5 January 1971 of the Punjab and Haryana High Court in Cr. A. 45 of 1968).
The Judgment was delivered by: BHAGWATI, J.
1.  The appellants and three
facts: The appellants and three others were tried before the Additional Sessions Judge, Hissar for offences under Sections 148, S. 302 read with S. 149 and S. 323 read with S. 149 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860.

The prosecution case was supported by the evidence of Surja, who was admittedly an eyewitness to the incident and relying on the evidence of Surja, the learned Additional Sessions Judge convicted the appellants and two of the other co-accused, namely, Kanshi Ram and Mani Ram of the offence u/s. 304 Part II read with S. 34 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 for causing the death of Khub Ram, and Kanshi Ram and Mani Ram also for the offence under S. 323 read with S. 34 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 for causing simple injuries to Surja.
During the pendency of these appeals, Kanshi Ram died and hence he was struck off from the record.
issues: What was the offence committed by the appellants?
petitioner_arguments: We do not see any reason to interfere with the concurrent view taken by the learned Additional Sessions Judge and the High Court in regard to the appreciation of such evidence.

It is, no doubt, true that there was some delay in the filing of the first information report by Surja and the explanation given for the delay does not appear to be very satisfactory, but that cannot by itself be a ground for disbelieving the prosecution evidence and particularly when if has been accepted both by the learned Additional Sessions Judge and the High Court.
respondent_arguments: The High Court took the view that the offence was one under S. 302 read with Section 34, since the injuries caused by the appellants were sufficient in the ordinary course of nature to cause death and the appellants did intend to cause these injuries.
It is amply supported by the decision of this Court in Virsa Singh v. State of Punjab 1958 Indlaw SC 821958 Indlaw SC 821958 Indlaw SC 82.
court_reasoning: We think the High Court was right in taking this view and it is amply supported by the decision of this Court in Virsa Singh v. State of Punjab 1958 Indlaw SC 821958 Indlaw SC 821958 Indlaw SC 82.

We do not, in the circumstances, see any reason to interfere with the conviction of the appellants, and if the offence for which they are convicted falls rightly within S. 302 read with Section 34, it is obvious that the life sentence imposed on the appellants, must be maintained.
holding: We accordingly confirm the conviction and sentence recorded against the appellants and dismiss the appeal.
